newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Soccer-Aldridge expects to play against Iceland.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Aldridge expects to play against Iceland.

text.p: Veteran striker John Aldridge said on Friday he will be fit to play for the Republic of Ireland against Iceland in a World Cup group eight qualifier at Lansdowne Road on Sunday (kick-off 1500 GMT).
Aldridge, 38, picked up a groin injury on Thursday while doing some work in the gym.
"It's only a niggle and I should be fine," Aldridge said.

Aldridge, who came on as a late substitute on the last occasion that the two sides met 10 years ago in a triangular tournament in Iceland, is expected to be partnered up-front by 34-year-old Olympicque Marseilles striker Tony Cascarino.
Regular Irish striker Niall Quinn misses the game as he has to undergo surgery next week to repair a torn cruciate ligament in his knee. He will miss the rest of the season.
Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane has returned to the squad after playing in just three of Ireland's last 20 internationals.
He was deployed as a defender for much of the Ireland squad training session on Thursday, a position he previously filled with English league club Nottingham Forest.
"I've seen him play often enough in midfield, I just thought that it would be interesting for a change to see how he would make out at the back," McCarthy said.
"It's an option I have to consider, particularly at a time when we have so much going for us in midfield," he added.
Ireland currently head group eight on goal difference from Romania, having won 5-0 away to Liechtenstein and 3-0 at home to Macedonia in their two opening games.
The visitors were beaten 4-0 at home to Romania in October while they also drew with Macedonia and lost to Lithuania.

Iceland's preparations for the trip to Dublin have been less than ideal because of injuries to several key players, a situation which forced national coach Logi Olafsson to make a number of changes to his 18-man squad.
Missing are twin brothers Arnar and Bjarki Gunnlaugsson as well as veteran striker Arnor Gudjohnsen.
Gudjohnsen's son, 18-year-old, Eidur Smari, will also be absent as he has not recovered from a double leg break sustained in a youth international against Ireland earlier this year.
Bolton Wanderers defender and team captain Gudni Bergsson failed a late fitness test.
The changes mean international recalls for midfielders Hlynur Birgisson and Hermann Hreidarsson.

Iceland are likely to have Birkir Kristinsson, who helped Norwegian club side Brann Bergen overcome Dutch side PSV Eindhoven and secure a place in the last eight of the European Cup Winners' Cup, in goal.
